relations.subject: eventing:function
relations.evidence: Buckets that are bound to an Eventing Function appear as a global JavaScript map. Map operations like GET, SET, and DELETE are exposed to the GET, SET, and DELETE Data Service provider operations.

relations.subject: eventing:basic-keyspace-accessor
relations.evidence: If the bucket binding has a wildcard `*` for its scope or collection, you cannot use a Basic Keyspace Accessor to access the Data Service. Instead, you must use an [Advanced Keyspace Accessor](#advanced%5Fbucket%5Faccessors).

relations.subject: eventing:function
relations.evidence: You can use top-level SQL++ keywords like SELECT, UPDATE, INSERT, and DELETE as inline words in Eventing Functions.

relations.subject: eventing:n1ql-function-call
relations.evidence: The `N1QL()` function has replaced the deprecated `N1qlQuery()`.

relations.subject: eventing:analytics-query-function
relations.evidence: The `couchbase.analyticsQuery()` function provides integration with SQL++ Analytics directly from the Eventing Service.

relations.subject: eventing:function
relations.evidence: Timers are asynchronously computed. They allow Eventing Functions to execute in reference to wall-clock events.

relations.subject: eventing:function
relations.evidence: The Timer callback handler is an entry point for the event when a timer, created by the specific Eventing Function, matures and fires.

relations.subject: eventing:asynchrony
relations.evidence: You can use Timers to add limited asynchrony back into your Function. Timers are designed specifically to prevent a state from being node-specific.

relations.subject: eventing:browser-extension
relations.evidence: You can use Timers instead of `setTimeout` and curl calls instead of `XMLHttpRequests`.

relations.subject: eventing:function
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate, applied to a newly-minted object
relations.evidence: The Eventing Service does not support importing libraries into Eventing Functions.

relations.subject: eventing:function
relations.evidence: The `OnUpdate` handler is called when you create or modify a document. The entry point `OnUpdate(doc, meta)` listens to mutations in the associated source bucket.

relations.subject: eventing:function
relations.evidence: The `OnDelete` handler is called when a document is deleted or removed due to expiration. The entry point `OnDelete(meta, options)` listens to mutations like deletions and expirations in the associated source bucket.

relations.subject: eventing:on-delete-handler
relations.evidence: You cannot get the value of a deleted or expired document.

relations.subject: eventing:on-delete-handler
relations.evidence: In versions of Couchbase Server before version 6.6.0, the optional argument `options` is not present and the entry point for the handler is `OnDelete(meta)`. The entry point is still supported, but using it means you're unable to differentiate deletion from expiration.

relations.subject: eventing:function
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate, applied to a newly-minted object
relations.evidence: The `OnDeploy` handler is invoked once when an Eventing function is deployed or resumed, before any mutations are processed. The entry point `OnDeploy(action)` is used for one-time setup tasks like resource initialization, creation of timers, and so on.

relations.subject: eventing:function
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate, applied to a newly-minted object
relations.evidence: You cannot use reserved words as variable names, function names, or JavaScript code properties in Eventing Functions.

relations.subject: eventing:function
relations.evidence: See [Advanced Keyspace Accessors](eventing-advanced-keyspace-accessors.md) for more details.

relations.subject: eventing:function
relations.evidence: See [Logging Functions](eventing-debugging-and-diagnosability.md#logging-functions) for more information.

relations.subject: eventing:function

relations.subject: eventing:function
relations.evidence: For more information about Timers, see [Timers](eventing-timers.md).

notable_absence.finding: No Enterprise/Community edition badge anywhere on this page, matching the Capella twin's own recorded absence. More specifically: this Server 8.0 page's analyticsQuery()/crc_64_go_iso()/base64 sections carry NO version-availability marker of any kind, in contrast to the Capella twin - see cross_product_finding. The only version fact stated anywhere on this page is the OnDelete(meta) vs OnDelete(meta, options) signature split at 6.6.0.

cross_component_finding: Two completeness gaps found in the Capella twin's extraction of the identical page structure: (1) eventing:library-imports was never minted despite 'Library Imports' being the fourth of four unsupported-feature headings the twin's own source bullet list names; this record mints it. (2) the twin recorded a `seeAlso` relation from eventing:crc-64-go-iso-function to the concept id eventing:crc64-function for what is actually a same-page anchor link (#crc64_call), not a cross-page Markdown link - inconsistent with the registry's own stated seeAlso convention ('Object is a PAGE ID, never a concept'; every occurrence is a structural link BETWEEN pages). This record does not repeat that relation, and flags it for cleanup during reconciliation. Separately, eventing:on-deploy-handler (minted independently in this batch's eventing-lifecycle.json) and the Capella twin's eventing:ondeploy-handler are the same concept under two spellings - a third instance of the exact id-fork pattern the registry already resolved once for eventing:on-update-handler/eventing:on-delete-handler (each of which folded an 'on<Verb>-handler' and an 'on-<verb>-handler' variant); not resolved here since reconciliation, not extraction, owns merges.
cross_product_finding: The Capella twin's analyticsQuery()/crc_64_go_iso()/base64() sections each carry a literal 'Couchbase Server 7.6' line immediately under the section heading (cloud/eventing/eventing-language-constructs.md, lines 234, 314 and 329 - confirmed by direct read, not inference), which round 8's extraction correctly captured as three availableSince relations. This Server 8.0 tree's OWN page for the identical three built-ins has NO such marker anywhere - grepping this page for '7.6' returns nothing. That is backwards from what you would expect: server/ is the tree that originates the version number (Capella runs on top of a Couchbase Server release and Capella's own docs are citing THAT number), yet it is the Capella copy that states it and the Server 8.0 original that has dropped it from its current-release documentation. A reader of this exact page in the Server 8.0 tree has no way to learn that analyticsQuery(), crc_64_go_iso() and the base64 function family are relatively recent (7.6+) additions rather than long-standing ones, unless they separately consult release notes or the Capella docs for the same feature.
